title: clampBudget NaN vulnerability breaks budgetRatio invariant
description: The clampBudget function does not handle non-numeric input, but the claimed invariant break is refuted by source-visible preventing layers.
claimed_root_cause: The clampBudget function at line 117 of useSimulationStore.ts performs Math.max(0.1, Math.min(0.4, ratio)) followed by Number(clamped.toFixed(2)). When ratio is non-numeric, Math.min(0.4, ratio) produces NaN, Math.max(0.1, NaN) produces NaN, and Number(NaN.toFixed(2)) produces NaN.

trace.description: setBudgetRatio calls clampBudget and assigns result to params.budgetRatio
clampBudget function definition at line 117: const clamped = Math.max(0.1, Math.min(0.4, ratio)); return Number(clamped.toFixed(2));
params.budgetRatio propagates to optimizer createSolverContext where Number.isFinite check defaults to 0.2

evidence.description: clampBudget function: const clamped = Math.max(0.1, Math.min(0.4, ratio)); return Number(clamped.toFixed(2));

reason: The optimizer's Number.isFinite(params.budgetRatio) guard at packages/engine/src/optimizer.ts:392 neutralizes NaN by falling back to DEFAULT_SIMULATION_PARAMS.budgetRatio (0.2), and the only caller of setBudgetRatio is ControlBar.tsx which uses a range input with min=10, max=40, step=5 ensuring only valid numeric values (0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, 0.35, 0.4) are ever passed.

title: evaluatePolicyGates overallStatus can give REVIEW when 4 of 5 policy gates pass
description: The evaluatePolicyGates function in gates.ts determines overall status as PASS only if passedCount >= 4 AND dominancePassed is true. If 4 out of 5 individual policy gates pass but COST_DOMINANCE fails, the overall status is REVIEW, which may mislead stakeholders about the optimization quality.
claimed_root_cause: The overallStatus logic in evaluatePolicyGates (gates.ts line 128) uses: if (!massPassed || !budgetPassed || passedCount <= 2) { FAIL } else if (passedCount >= 4 && dominancePassed) { PASS } else { REVIEW }. When exactly 4 gates pass and dominancePassed is the 5th that fails, status is REVIEW despite near-complete gate compliance.

trace.description: evaluatePolicyGates called with {reactive, sennagrid, hubCentrality, weeklyQuotaK} at end of optimizeResourceAllocation
overallStatus is set based on massPassed, budgetPassed, passedCount, and dominancePassed at lines 128-132

evidence.description: evaluatePolicyGates function: const overallStatus = REVIEW; if (!massPassed || !budgetPassed || passedCount <= 2) { overallStatus = FAIL; } else if (passedCount >= 4 && dominancePassed) { overallStatus = PASS; } else { overallStatus = REVIEW; }
evaluatePolicyGates called at line 639 with results from full optimization run

reason: Source-grounded: the evaluatePolicyGates function in packages/engine/src/gates.ts lines 127-132 explicitly implements the tri-status classification (FAIL/REVIEW/PASS) as documented intent. When passedCount >= 4 and dominancePassed is false (with massPassed and budgetPassed true), REVIEW is the correct output per the if/else-if chain. This is intentional design, not a bug or invariant failure.
